source_checks.finding: Under Find your files, subsection Search from File Explorer, the page says: To find files stored inside a folder, search from a folder like Downloads. It also says: Select File explorer from the taskbar. Applies To lists Windows 11 and Windows 10. Excerpt and step match. The page gives no search box location, so the target correctly does not add one.

The page says: This view displays all 6 known Windows folders, listing Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, and Videos. Applies To lists Windows 11 and Windows 10. The sentence is on the page, but the fetch did not confirm it sits under the cited heading Restore known folders if you have unpinned them.

Under Restore known folders if you have unpinned them, the page gives four steps: Select Start > File Explorer, or the File Explorer icon in the taskbar; Select Home in the left navigation pane; Select the Up arrow from the navigation buttons available to the left of the address bar; Select and hold (or right-click) on the folder and select Pin to Quick access from the context menu. Applies To lists Windows 11 and Windows 10. Supports the restore steps, but only as a condition for a folder that was unpinned.

Section Find a list of files you've downloaded supports: At the top right, click More, then Downloads, in Chrome. The text is accurate, but it does not apply here: the user never mentioned Chrome, and the target correctly leaves it out. The section has no Applies To line.

required_actions.action: Open File Explorer from the taskbar
Search inside the Downloads folder for the emailed attachment
If Downloads is missing from Quick access after it was unpinned, pin it back (Home, Up arrow, select and hold or right-click Downloads, Pin to Quick access)

findings: factual_steps_labels_contacts_claims: the target says If Downloads is not in Quick access because it was unpinned. The source only says if you have unpinned a folder such as Downloads. The target therefore states a cause the passage does not establish, and the user never said they unpinned it.

one_action_per_step: the restore sequence is one run-on sentence (select Home in the left navigation pane, select the Up arrow to the left of the address bar, then select and hold (or right-click) Downloads and select Pin to Quick access). It packs four actions into one step.
